title: Common API clients
description: Server-only TypeScript clients for GitHub, Stripe Checkout, Resend, Supabase reads, Microsoft Graph, Google Calendar, OpenAI, Anthropic, Saleor catalog reads, and Steel sessions with explicit credentials and bounded HTTP transport.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and a server runtime with standard Fetch, AbortController, streams, TextEncoder, and TextDecoder; Node.js 22+ is the supported baseline.
No runtime packages, environment reads, OAuth flows, account setup, or live connections occur at install/import time.
Keep credentialed clients and their injected resolvers in server-only code; this module is not a browser bundle or a native credential vault.
Provider models, versions, scopes, tenant policy, billing limits, data schemas, and live integration acceptance belong to the consuming application.

configuration: Inject trusted token resolvers and Fetch configuration; never copy request headers, request JSON, user URLs, or client-supplied identity into client configuration.
GitHub, Stripe, and Anthropic require an explicit supported API version; AI adapters also require a configured model and output token limit.
Stripe requires approved server price mappings, return URLs, an order authorization callback, and a persisted idempotency key per attempt.
Resend requires a verified server-owned sender, exact recipient/content authorization, and a persisted idempotency key per delivery event.
Supabase requires a project HTTPS origin, publishable key, caller user token, and table/column allowlists; enable and test RLS in the target database.
Graph requires a delegated Graph token; Calendar requires allowed calendar IDs and explicit time bounds; these clients do not obtain or refresh OAuth tokens.
Model calls require a mandatory application authorization callback; check tenant, data disclosure, and budget before allowing each paid call.
Saleor requires a trusted GraphQL endpoint; Steel requires explicit authority for each session operation and careful handling of server-only connection URLs.
limitations: An API client does not provision SSO, connect user accounts, refresh tokens, create services, or grant spending authority.
No retries, durable idempotency store, webhook receiver, signature verification, email delivery reconciliation, billing entitlement processing, or job queue is included.
The transport enforces an exact trusted HTTPS origin, not DNS/IP egress isolation. The receiving environment must restrict outbound destinations and use a standards-compliant Fetch implementation.

Only the documented operations are implemented. Supabase service-role reads, Stripe custom Checkout domains, streaming AI/tools, full calendar synchronization, Saleor checkout, and browser navigation are outside this module.
Tests replace only the outbound HTTP boundary and make no live calls. Provider credentials, current permissions, database policies, actual payments/delivery, and deployed behavior remain unverified.
